function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute shell commands on a Linux environment. Filesystem usually persists between calls.

Do NOT use cat/head/tail to read files — use read_file instead.
Do NOT use grep/rg/find to search — use search_files instead.
Do NOT use ls to list directories — use search_files(target='files') instead.
Do NOT use sed/awk to edit files — use patch instead.
Do NOT use echo/cat heredoc to create files — use write_file instead.
Reserve terminal for: builds, installs, git, processes, scripts, network, package managers, and anything that needs a shell.

Foreground (default): Commands return INSTANTLY when done, even if the timeout is high. Set timeout=300 for long builds/scripts — you'll still get the result in seconds if it's fast. Prefer foreground for short commands.
Background: Set background=true to get a session_id. Two patterns:
  (1) Long-lived processes that never exit (servers, watchers).
  (2) Long-running tasks with notify_on_complete=true — you can keep working on other things and the system auto-notifies you when the task finishes. Great for test suites, builds, deployments, or anything that takes more than a minute.
For servers/watchers, do NOT use shell-level background wrappers (nohup/disown/setsid/trailing '&') in foreground mode. Use background=true so Hermes can track lifecycle and output.
After starting a server, verify readiness with a health check or log signal, then run tests in a separate terminal() call. Avoid blind sleep loops.
Use process(action="poll") for progress checks, process(action="wait") to block until done.
Working directory: Use 'workdir' for per-command cwd.
PTY mode: Set pty=true for interactive CLI tools (Codex, Claude Code, Python REPL).

Do NOT use vim/nano/interactive tools without pty=true — they hang without a pseudo-terminal. Pipe git output to cat if it might page.

command.description: The command to execute on the VM

background.description: Run the command in the background. Two patterns: (1) Long-lived processes that never exit (servers, watchers). (2) Long-running tasks paired with notify_on_complete=true — you can keep working and get notified when the task finishes. For short commands, prefer foreground with a generous timeout instead.

timeout.description: Max seconds to wait (default: 180, foreground max: 600). Returns INSTANTLY when command finishes — set high for long tasks, you won't wait unnecessarily. Foreground timeout above 600s is rejected; use background=true for longer commands.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command (absolute path). Defaults to the session working directory.

pty.description: Run in pseudo-terminal (PTY) mode for interactive CLI tools like Codex, Claude Code, or Python REPL. Only works with local and SSH backends. Default: false.

notify_on_complete.description: When true (and background=true), you'll be automatically notified exactly once when the process finishes. **This is the right choice for almost every long-running task** — tests, builds, deployments, multi-item batch jobs, anything that takes over a minute and has a defined end. Use this and keep working on other things; the system notifies you on exit. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with watch_patterns — when both are set, watch_patterns is dropped.

watch_patterns.description: Strings to watch for in background process output. HARD RATE LIMIT: at most 1 notification per 15 seconds per process — matches arriving inside the cooldown are dropped. After 3 consecutive 15-second windows with dropped matches, watch_patterns is automatically disabled for that process and promoted to notify_on_complete behavior (one notification on exit, no more mid-process spam). USE ONLY for truly rare, one-shot mid-process signals on LONG-LIVED processes that will never exit on their own — e.g. ['Application startup complete'] on a server so you know when to hit its endpoint, or ['migration done'] on a daemon. DO NOT use for: (1) end-of-run markers like 'DONE'/'PASS' — use notify_on_complete instead; (2) error patterns like 'ERROR'/'Traceback' in loops or multi-item batch jobs — they fire on every iteration and you'll hit the strike limit fast; (3) anything you'd ever combine with notify_on_complete. When in doubt, choose notify_on_complete. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with notify_on_complete — set one, not both.

## What I did
- Checked live web/API availability for public/free martial arts technique/drill data sources.
- Verified several no-auth endpoints directly: Wikipedia MediaWiki API, Wikidata API, Commons API, GitHub raw/API, Hugging Face dataset API, Figshare API.
- Looked for options that can be integrated now without credentials and noted sources that may need accounts later.

## Findings

| Source | URL / API | Auth needed? | Usefulness for CombatAtlas | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| **Wikipedia / MediaWiki category data** | Category API: `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&list=categorymembers&cmtitle=Category:Martial_arts_techniques&cmlimit=500&format=json` | **No** | **High for seed technique index** | Returned 88 technique pages in live test, e.g. `Front kick`, `Joint lock`, `Ippon seoi nage`, `Chokehold`, etc. Can also fetch summaries/extracts/images via MediaWiki/Page Summary APIs. Content is CC BY-SA, so attribution/share-alike matters. |
| **Wikidata** | Search/API: `https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities&search=armbar&language=en&format=json` and SPARQL endpoint `https://query.wikidata.org/sparql` | **No** | **Medium-high for structured metadata** | Useful for entity IDs, aliases, links to Wikipedia pages, categories, related concepts, multilingual names. Coverage is inconsistent for drills, better for named techniques/styles. |
| **Wikimedia Commons** | `https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/api.php` | **No** | **Medium for images/media** | Can find technique photos/diagrams with licenses. Need store attribution/license metadata. Not a drill database by itself. |
| **GitHub: ubershmekel/bjjdata** | `https://github.com/ubershmekel/bjjdata` | **No** | **Medium for BJJ/grappling examples** | MIT licensed per README. Contains markdown entries with YouTube links, dates, people, clip timestamps, tags like `armbar`, `joint-lock`, `gi`. More match-clip metadata than instructional drill descriptions. Good optional enrichment. |
| **Kaggle: Grappling Techniques dataset** | `https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/liiucbs/grappling-techniques` | **Likely Kaggle account/API token for download** | **Potentially high, but do not block on it** | Referenced by GitHub project as Apache 2.0 and covering BJJ/Judo/Wrestling techniques. | **GitHub: Grappling-Technique-Analytics** | `https://github.com/omeedtavakoli/Grappling-Technique-Analytics` | **No for repo** | **Low-medium** | Does not appear to include the dataset itself, but confirms Kaggle source/license claim and gives analysis ideas. |

Live check showed it is mostly QA/instruction text about MMA/BJJ, not a clean technique/drill catalog. Could be ignored or used only for glossary/RAG experiments. |
| **Figshare: Kyokushin karate motion capture dataset** | Collection API: `https://api.figshare.com/v2/collections/4981073` | **No** | **Medium for advanced motion/media features, low for searchable drill text** | CC0 datasets with downloadable ZIPs: “Multimodal dataset of 37 Kyokushin karate athletes” and one-athlete dataset. Great legal source for karate motion data, but heavy and not directly technique descriptions. |
| **MADS: Martial Arts, Dancing and Sports Dataset** | `http://visal.cs.cityu.edu.hk/research/mads/` | **No obvious API; Google Drive download** | **Low-medium** | Academic video/pose dataset. Includes martial arts actions, but README says copyright City University of Hong Kong; license unclear. Use only for research/prototyping unless license clarified. |

## Recommended integration strategy

1. **Build now with no credentials**
   - Create a local seed/import script using:
     - Wikipedia category `Category:Martial arts techniques`
     - Wikipedia page summaries/extracts
     - Wikidata entity lookup for aliases/IDs
   - Store normalized records locally, e.g.:
     ```ts
     {
       name,
       slug,
       source: "wikipedia",
       sourceUrl,
       summary,
       aliases,
       martialArts,
       tags,
       license: "CC BY-SA",
       attribution
     }
     ```

2. **Treat external APIs as import-time sources, not runtime dependencies**
   - Fetch/cache data during development/build/admin import.
   - App search should work from the local database even if APIs are down or keys are missing.

3. **Add optional enrichers**
   - GitHub `bjjdata`: import MIT-licensed BJJ clip/tag metadata as examples, not core instructional content.
   - Wikimedia Commons: add licensed images with attribution.
   - Figshare karate motion capture: keep as future advanced/media dataset, not initial search content.
   - Kaggle Grappling Techniques: add later behind optional `KAGGLE_USERNAME` / `KAGGLE_KEY`.

4. **Avoid blockers**
   - Do **not** depend on Balldontlie/API-Sports; they are sports statistics APIs, not useful drill/technique catalogs.
   - Do **not** require Kaggle credentials for the first version.

## Files created or modified
- None.

## Issues encountered
- No general web-search API tool was available, so I used direct live HTTP checks from the terminal.
- Some promising academic datasets are legal/technical mismatches for an app database: useful for ML/motion research, less useful for user-facing drill descriptions.
- License obligations matter:
  - Wikipedia/Wikidata/Wikimedia require attribution and, for Wikipedia text, CC BY-SA compliance.
  - GitHub `bjjdata` is MIT.
  - Figshare karate files checked as CC0.
  - MADS license is unclear despite public download.

## Recommended integration strategy

1. **Build now with no credentials**
   - Create a local seed/import script using:
     - Wikipedia category `Category:Martial arts techniques`
     - Wikipedia page summaries/extracts
     - Wikidata entity lookup for aliases/IDs
   - Store normalized records locally, e.g.:
     ```ts
     {
       name,
       slug,
       source: "wikipedia",
       sourceUrl,
       summary,
       aliases,
       martialArts,
       tags,
       license: "CC BY-SA",
       attribution
     }
     ```

2. **Treat external APIs as import-time sources, not runtime dependencies**
   - Fetch/cache data during development/build/admin import.
   - App search should work from the local database even if APIs are down or keys are missing.

3. **Add optional enrichers**
   - GitHub `bjjdata`: import MIT-licensed BJJ clip/tag metadata as examples, not core instructional content.
   - Wikimedia Commons: add licensed images with attribution.
   - Figshare karate motion capture: keep as future advanced/media dataset, not initial search content.
   - Kaggle Grappling Techniques: add later behind optional `KAGGLE_USERNAME` / `KAGGLE_KEY`.

4. **Avoid blockers**
   - Do **not** depend on Balldontlie/API-Sports; they are sports statistics APIs, not useful drill/technique catalogs.
   - Do **not** require Kaggle credentials for the first version.
